title: Micro-segmented GPU memory ledger + opportunistic KV GC for mixed inference workloads
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: OOMs and conservative weight/KV/activation reservations limit cluster utilization. Existing coarse-grained slabs either leave unused KV capacity when activations spike or cause expensive weight preemption. Goal: design and implement a micro-segmentation memory ledger plus an opportunistic KV garbage collector that reclaims stale KV entries and temporarily repurposes small memory segments for short-term activation bursts without violating per-tenant isolation guarantees. The approach should be compatible with continuous batching and require minimal changes to customer configs. Success metrics: reduce OOM incidents related to KV pressure by >=90% in canary clusters, improve average GPU memory utilization by 12-20% for mixed short/long-sequence workloads, and keep 95th token-latency regression <5% for P95 workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented micro-segmentation ledger that exposes per-segment ownership (weight, kv, activation) and supports fast reassignment with accounting events
Opportunistic KV GC engine that runs in runtime and supports token-age LRU + sequence-length-aware priority, with configurable aggressiveness per cluster
Integration with continuous batching so batch admission checks consider reclaimable segments and schedule eviction/compaction without stalling healthy requests
Telemetry: new events for segment_reassign, kv_gc_reclaimed_bytes, kv_eviction_reason, and debt_tokens; dashboards + alert when reclaim rate or latency impact exceed thresholds
Canary rollout (5% of capacity) with no increase in customer-facing OOMs and documented rollback path
Unit + integration tests that simulate mixed footprints and confirm memory invariants and no memory safety regressions
tasks: Design doc and API for segment ledger (owner, size, age, flags)
Implement lightweight per-GPU segment headers and atomic transfer ops
KV GC: implement token-age LRU + sequence-length priority; expose runtime knobs
Admission path changes in batch scheduler to consult reclaimable pool
Metrics/telemetry and dashboard for reclaimed bytes, GC latency, and eviction counts
E2E canary deployment and load test harness with synthetic mixed footprint workload
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal dev clusters - enable ledger + gc with conservative knobs (low aggressiveness)
Stage 2: Canary - enable on 5% of hosted capacity, monitor reclaim metrics and latency for 72h
Stage 3: Gradual ramp - increase to 25% if canary stable; run heavy continuous-batching tests
Stage 4: Full rollout with configurable default aggressiveness and tenant opt-out flag
risks: Over-aggressive GC could increase tail latency for active chat sessions if we evict hot KV entries; mitigated by token-age heuristics and conservative default knobs
Frequent segment churn may increase fragmentation; we will add periodic compaction and fragmentation gauge
Race conditions during atomic segment transfers across threads — requires careful lock-free primitives and thorough stress tests
Telemetry gaps early in rollout could delay detection of regressions; require immediate dashboarding before canary
